name: JW Marriott Desert Springs Resort & Spa
positioning: Palm Desert resort on 450 acres of desert gardens and lakes, with two championship golf courses, a tennis club and a 38,000-square-foot spa
best_for: Families wanting arcade games, mini golf and boat tours

facts.text: The resort sits on 450 acres of desert gardens.
The resort's lakes are home to swans and pink flamingos.
Desert Springs Golf Club has two championship courses, the Palm and the Valley, designed by Ted Robinson.
The resort has an 18-hole natural turf putting course with bunkers, lakes, streams and waterfalls.
The tennis facility has hard, clay and grass courts.
The resort's tennis program is run by Peter Burwash International for every skill level.
Spa Desert Springs is a 38,000-square-foot facility with an Aromatherapy Hammam Steam Chamber.
The spa has an outdoor saltwater lap pool and a coed Wellness Lounge.
Rooms feature plush bedding, hardwood floors, modern furnishings and mountain-inspired murals in blue, gray and white.
The resort has five outdoor pools.
The resort is minutes from Acrisure Arena, the Living Desert Zoo & Garden and the Indian Wells Tennis Garden.
Rockwood Grill has water views from its patio.

highlights.text: The spa's VIP Sanctuary Spa Suite is staffed by a personal butler and has a private entrance and a hydrotherapy tub in a private courtyard.
Guided boat tours through the resort's waterways depart from the lobby.
Frank Sinatra's last public performance took place at the resort.
The JW Entertainment Zone is an arcade with new and retro games and duckpin bowling.
The Vice Presidential Suite has views of the Santa Rosa Mountains and the Coachella Valley.

considerations.text: A daily resort fee applies and covers amenities such as range access, mini golf, bike rental and court time.
WhataHotel notes the desert location may feel remote for some travelers.
